newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Pernas to complete restructuring in Oct.
newsitem.headline: Pernas to complete restructuring in Oct.

text.p: Pernas International Holdings Bhd (PIHB) said on Friday its restructuring exercise that will transform the company into a diversified group is expected to be completed by next month.

"We hope to complete the exercise by the middle of October and to list the new shares and warrants (on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange) in December," PIHB chairman Tunku Shahriman Tunku Sulaiman told reporters after the company's extraordinary general meeting (EGM).
PIHB is acquiring assets of state investment firm Perbadanan Nasional Bhd (Pernas) for 1.15 billion ringgit in the country's third largest privatisation.
PIHB will pay for Pernas' assets by issuing 250 million new PIHB shares at 2.40 ringgit per share and with 546 million ringgit in cash from proceeds of a 250 million ringgit bond issue with warrants.
At the EGM, shareholders unanimously approved the proposals, Tunku Shahriman said.
PIHB had earlier received approval from the securities industry watchdog, the Securities Commission.
Tunku Shahriman is also leading a group which has bought a controlling 32 percent stake in the enlarged PIHB for 495 million ringgit in a management buyout.

The privatisation exercise will see PIHB, whose investments had been in property and hotels, venturing into trading and manufacturing, financial services, plantations, property development and construction and engineering.
The privatisation ranks behind state-run utilities Telekom Malaysia and Tenaga Nasional, which were allowed to sell shares on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange earlier this decade.

Tunku Shahriman has said that PIHB is aiming for a pre-tax profit of 500 million ringgit by the year 2000. For the financial year ended January 31, 1996, it reported a pre-tax profit of 70.74 million ringgit against 64.28 million in the previous year.
